profile.summary: This record is one paper's evaluation built on the POISK dataset, a collection of antibody sequences and binding metadata extracted from patent filings by a large language model pipeline. The evaluation treats structure prediction models as zero-shot binder classifiers: for each antibody and antigen pair the model folds the complex and its interface confidence scores, ipTM and ipSAE, are used to rank patent-supported binders against putative non-binders for the same antigen. The released folding metrics cover six co-folding models with 22,494 rows each. The paper itself is a bioRxiv preprint that this pass could not fetch, so this page is written from the Zenodo release and is deliberately thin on results.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Whether a co-folding model's confidence in the interface it builds can tell a real antibody-antigen pair from a plausible but non-binding one, without any training for that task. The quantity used is not a predicted affinity but a structural confidence score, ipTM or an ipSAE-style score, so the output is a ranking rather than a measurement. The release warns that a score must be read with the chain pair it was computed on: each ipSAE-style score ships beside a column naming that pair, and a value whose pair is not antibody against antigen is not a binding metric.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: The underlying data are extracted from patent text rather than curated from a database. The release is a flat CSV of 93,193 rows and 47 columns, one row per unique record, carrying variable region sequences for the heavy and light chains, the target sequence with its provenance (what the release holds, what the patent's GenBank deposit holds and what the named UniProt entry holds), target metadata including gene symbols, UniProt identifiers and source organisms, experimental binding affinities with assay methods such as surface plasmon resonance and biolayer interferometry, and epitope information including linear ranges and structural contact residues. Extraction was done by a pipeline driven by large language models, with both prompts published verbatim: an extractor prompt run once per patent and an auditor prompt run once per record to re-locate its support in the patent.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: The released folding metrics are the evaluation's raw material: one CSV per model for six models, 22,494 rows each, sharing 28 columns whose order differs between files, so a user must align on names rather than position. The metrics include ipTM and ipSAE, and each ipSAE-style score carries the chain pair it was computed on, including a variant that treats the antibody as a single chain. The archives also hold the predicted structures and the predicted aligned error arrays for each model. A caveat the release states plainly is that these predictions were run against dataset version 1.0.1, not against the version 1.1 release they sit beside, so a pairing of metrics to records has to account for the version change, which the release describes as correcting errors found in 1.0.1.

sections.title: What the release says about its own reliability
sections.body: The release is explicit that the labels come from a generative pipeline and may be wrong. It warns that large language model extraction is subject to hallucinations, naming the misassociation of affinity values with antibody variants and errors in residue indexing as the discrepancies to expect. Against that it ships an audit layer with three columns: a verdict in three tiers, where CONFIRMED means every field was explicitly supported by the patent text, PLAUSIBLE means nothing contradicted the record but support was partial, indirect or inferred, and REVIEW means the record appeared incorrect or could not be established and a human should look, which the release says is not an assertion that the row is false; a flags column naming fields with potential mismatches; and a reasoning column explaining how the value was reached. Users are told to verify critical sequences or affinity data against the original patent before any experimental work.

facts.label: Datasets
facts.value: One release in two parts. The dataset table is 93,193 rows and 47 columns in version 1.1, one row per unique record. The benchmark's folding side is six per-model metric CSVs of 22,494 rows each, with the predicted structures and predicted aligned error arrays archived beside them for af2m, boltz, intellifold, of3, protenix and protenix_v2. The folding predictions were run against version 1.0.1 of the table rather than the 1.1 release.

facts.label: Splits
facts.value: Evaluation only, with no training, validation or test division: the models are used zero-shot and every pair is folded and scored. The release publishes no split manifest and no pair list; the folding metrics are a flat table of 22,494 rows per model, and how those rows pair binders with putative non-binders is not described in the Zenodo record.

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: Interface confidence scores from the folding models, used as a ranking signal, so higher means a more confident predicted interface: ipTM and ipSAE-style scores, the latter reported per chain pair, including a variant that treats the antibody as a single chain. Each metric CSV holds 28 columns. The release stresses that no score is a binding measurement and that a score computed on a chain pair other than antibody against antigen is not a binding metric at all.

notes: Written from the Zenodo release only. The paper is a bioRxiv preprint and this run is not permitted to request bioRxiv; its PDF address, for a later pass, is https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.10.24.761513v1.full.pdf. As a result this page states no result, no pair count and no description of the negatives: the record's stored attributes describe 22,494 complexes as 11,247 pairs, with 7,647 nearest-CDR matches from the Observed Antibody Space and 3,600 germline-reverted decoys, and a 95 per cent identity exclusion against SAbDab, but none of that is in a file saved here, so it is left off the page and the leakage, split and uncertainty facts are marked unextracted. Three counts must be kept apart and only two are supported here: 93,193 rows is the version 1.1 dataset table, and 22,494 rows is each model's folding metric CSV; the 89,074-record figure for version 1.0.1 is not in the saved record. The folding predictions were run against version 1.0.1 while the release is 1.1, which corrects errors in 1.0.1, so metric rows and dataset rows do not join cleanly. released is the Zenodo publication_date field, not a last-modified timestamp. No code or leaderboard exists, so code_url and results_url are null.
